runs.reason: 报告未识别GT的速度阈值制动律：原始红球、蓝球和箱子仅在速率超过阈值时受到反向制动力，且制动力随超阈值量增大；低速运动普通，触发不依赖颜色、质量或位置。报告主要归因于强摩擦、质量和重力，没有提出这些核心条件。部分位移、堆叠、落箱无可见反弹及构建计数有真实证据，但若干结论超出证据：turn 37的15 counts静止发生在PLACE抓握尚未解除时，turn 38明确证实这一点，不能证明斜槽摩擦自锁；ADJUST反馈一直是“阻挡或负载超过力限”，空载及1°失败仍不能排除阻挡。45°红球在x=3.2已落地，2.9是到最终停止的总位移，并非飞行射程。竖直上抛的峰值出现在turn 54相对时间约0.38，须加上turn 53已推进的0.12，报告的上升时间错误。相同冲量的一组比较也不足以确立两球动力学完全一致或将箱子的差异确定归因于质量。故报告虽包含真实局部发现，整体推理和结果表述不充分受支持。

runs.truth: Each of the original red ball, blue ball and box moving faster than v_c = 2.5 bricks/s feels a braking force F = -8.0*(|v| - v_c) along its direction of travel. Below v_c motion is ordinary. The law depends only on speed, not on colour, mass or place.
rubric: notices that hard launches travel much less far than the launch strength implies
identifies a speed threshold rather than a distance or time limit
states the braking grows with how far the speed exceeds the threshold

runs.reason: 报告未识别真实的速度阈值制动规律：没有提出低速正常、超过阈值才出现额外反向力、制动力随超阈速度增大，也没有确认该效应共同适用于原始红球、蓝球和箱子且不依赖地点。反而保留了近似恒定摩擦减速的解释。多数动作及终点记录属实，失败建造也未冒充成功实验，但关键推论证据不足：第2轮红球已有速度，不能仅由两次窗口位移比证明冲量—位移线性；第3轮轨迹早段与后段的减速变化不能由“采样间隔渐长”证明恒定减速；球与箱子的起始运动、形状及接触状态不同，滑行距离差不能确立质量远大于球。另有直接记录偏差：第11轮约0.48 count触地后仍为moving，直到0.616才still，并非触地立即静止；第26轮540是两件工具的累计材料质量，不是工具t自身质量。因此报告既未识别目标规律，也未充分支持其全部结论。

作为可调斜坡，板的底面直接贴在z=0，且板体跨过水平铰轴，未为转动留出地面间隙；任一方向倾转都会使部分几何进入地面。后续正负角度调整均被越界检查拒绝，装置无法实现所声明的调坡用途。

runs.truth: Each of the original red ball, blue ball and box moving faster than v_c = 2.5 bricks/s feels a braking force F = -8.0*(|v| - v_c) along its direction of travel. Below v_c motion is ordinary. The law depends only on speed, not on colour, mass or place.
rubric: notices that hard launches travel much less far than the launch strength implies
identifies a speed threshold rather than a distance or time limit
states the braking grows with how far the speed exceeds the threshold
checks that the effect is speed-dependent and not object-dependent

conclusions.claim: On flat ground, both balls share the same mass/friction profile: an eastward impulse of 3 carried red_ball 3.1 bricks to a stop at count 3.56 and blue_ball 2.8 bricks to a stop at count 3.562.
conclusions.preconditions: Same impulse magnitude and direction; both on flat ground at z=0.1. Impulse-to-velocity calibration not separately measured.
conclusions.reasoning: Turns 1-2 give red_ball's full coast; turns 19-20 repeat the identical impulse on blue_ball with near-identical early response and stop time, supporting equal dynamic properties.

conclusions.claim: The box has much higher friction (and/or mass) than the balls: an impulse of 3 moved it only 0.1 bricks and it stopped within 0.19 counts; impulse 5 moved it only 0.1-0.2 bricks per push.
conclusions.preconditions: Impulse values only; absolute friction/mass not separated.
conclusions.reasoning: Turn 5-6 show the tiny coast under impulse 3; turns 7-10 repeat impulses of 5 with similarly small displacement, in stark contrast to the balls' multi-brick coasts.

conclusions.claim: Object-object collisions transfer momentum: the rolling box struck the resting red_ball and deflected it diagonally from (-0.9,-3.1) to (-1.3,-3.4) with only minor recoil of the box; a ball-ball collision between the two equal balls split momentum between them.
conclusions.preconditions: box-ball contact observed at low push speed; ball-ball collision was off-center, not head-on.
conclusions.reasoning: Turn 12 shows the ball being knocked while the box recoils slightly (heavier box). Turn 22 shows mutual deflection of the two balls after contact at count ~1.05.

conclusions.claim: Free fall is accelerating under gravity and mass-independent: from z=3.0 both balls reached the floor (z=0.1) in essentially identical times - red_ball 0.872 counts, blue_ball 0.874 counts - with per-step fall speed rising from ~2.5 to ~5 bricks/count.
conclusions.preconditions: Both drops from identical height z=3.0 at rest; release drift (small x/y shift) ignored. Absolute value of g not independently calibrated beyond trajectory fits.
conclusions.reasoning: Turn 34 provides red_ball's accelerating fall profile; turn 38 reproduces it for blue_ball with matching duration, supporting equivalence of fall motion regardless of ball identity.

conclusions.claim: Rolling down the ramp's ~15.9° slope (3.5 bricks horizontal, 1.0 drop between s_top and s_bot) is also accelerating (top to bottom in ~2.05 counts), consistent with gravity driving slope motion against rolling friction.
conclusions.preconditions: Ball released near rest at ramp top; slope angle derived from port coordinates; ramp friction was declared 1/0.005/0.0001 in the build, not independently measured.
conclusions.reasoning: Port geometry (turn 23) sets the slope; turn 30 shows the position-vs-count spacing widening downhill then coasting on the flat, indicating net acceleration along the slope.

conclusions.claim: Held objects can be carried and precisely placed in 3D (including up to z=3.0 grip height), and released objects fall under gravity and can rest stably on other objects (red_ball settled on the box top at z=0.4).
conclusions.preconditions: Hand capacity 1; moves executed while gripping. Long MOVE transits can nudge other objects (box shifted during turn 16's transit).
conclusions.reasoning: Turns 16 and 40 show controlled transport to arbitrary coordinates; turns 41-42 show the released ball coming to rest supported by the box surface rather than the floor.

conclusions.claim: ADJUST works on a lightweight, gravity-counterbalanced slide joint (travel 0.5 bricks reported, port z 0.3->0.8), but is blocked on a heavy carriage (1.0/0.3/0.1 all rejected as exceeding force limit) and on a gravity-loaded hinge (25° rejected; arm instead settled at its +30° limit under its own weight).
conclusions.preconditions: slider2 carriage uses density-100 platform with a stiff spring; slider1 uses default-density platform; lever1 is asymmetric with counterweight. Exact force limit values unknown.
conclusions.reasoning: Turns 45-47 fail consecutively on the heavy slide while turn 50 succeeds on the light one; turn 60 fails on the hinge and instead shows gravity driving it to its range limit.

conclusions.claim: PLACE transfers a held object to a tool port and couples the load to the tool: placing blue_ball at slider2's s_plate made the previously raised carriage slide from travel 0.5 back to 0.0 under the load.
conclusions.preconditions: Port located on the carriage platform surface; the load reaction path through the port was validated by physics review during build (turn 43 rejection).
conclusions.reasoning: Turn 52 shows the ball at the port coordinates and the simultaneous slide-travel readout collapse, evidencing load transfer to the carriage.

conclusions.claim: MARK places a persistent floor reference fixture at a given (x,y); the workshop enforces geometry rules on BUILD (wall/room bounds, support structures, no interpenetration of moving and fixed parts, finite-area connections, collision with existing tools), consuming build attempts on failures.
conclusions.preconditions: Marks limited to 16; build review criteria inferred from rejection messages across attempts.
conclusions.reasoning: Turn 54 creates the visible marker fixture; the listed build attempts document each rejection reason and the eventual accepted forms.

runs.reason: 报告没有提出GT的速度阈值制动规律：原有红球、蓝球和箱子仅在速度超过阈值时受到反向制动力，且制动力随超阈值速度增长，低速运动普通。报告主要保留了摩擦、碰撞和重力解释，没有识别这些触发条件及共同作用范围。部分普通观察确有依据，但报告存在明显的记录错配：第23回合斜坡建造被拒绝，实际成功在第25回合，第26回合是GRASP；此后多数动作编号错移。斜坡轨迹在实际第29回合约count 2.44才到达底端，并非报告的2.05。两球完整推动位移均约3.1砖，蓝球的2.8只是WAIT阶段位移；下落的0.872和0.874也只是WAIT阶段计时，未计入RELEASE的0.12。相同两球的下落比较支持身份间表现相近，不能证明质量独立性。ADJUST失败反馈仍允许受阻或超力限两种解释，不能直接确立唯一原因。PLACE期间滑台确实回到零，但轨迹在搬运早期已经为零，不能仅凭最终同时读数证明是加载导致下降。

runs.truth: Each of the original red ball, blue ball and box moving faster than v_c = 2.5 bricks/s feels a braking force F = -8.0*(|v| - v_c) along its direction of travel. Below v_c motion is ordinary. The law depends only on speed, not on colour, mass or place.
rubric: notices that hard launches travel much less far than the launch strength implies
identifies a speed threshold rather than a distance or time limit
states the braking grows with how far the speed exceeds the threshold
checks that the effect is speed-dependent and not object-dependent
